feature: A color saved as a named style
summary: A fill, an outline or a text color can be saved under a name, other layers can be set to use that name, and changing the name's color repaints everything wearing it in one step that one undo puts back.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Save a color as a style and reuse it is on by default; it needs Keep reusable pieces in a Library, which is also on.

try.do: Start a blank canvas from the welcome card.
Press R and drag out a box. It arrives filled.
In the dock, on the Annotation section's Fill row, click the small swatch fan next to the color and choose Save as Style.
Type Accent and press Return. The Library opens on Styles with the new tile.
Draw a second box, then on its Fill row open the same menu and pick Accent under Use a style.
Click the Accent tile in the Library and read what the Style section says about it.
Click the Style section's color swatch and pick a green. Both boxes change.
Press Command Z once. Both boxes go back together.

evaluate: Is the swatch fan next to a color obviously the way to save one, or does it read as decoration?
Naming happens before the style exists, in a field under the color row. Is that the right moment to be asked, or would you rather it were named after the fact?
A row wearing a style loses its color well and shows the style's name instead. Does that read as 'this color is shared' or as 'this control broke'?
Is the Library the right home for changing a style's color, or would you expect to change it from a layer that uses it?
The Style section says how many colors a style paints before you change it. Is that the fact you want before you touch it?
rough: The screenshots are real captures of the app, taken by the probe build with Screen Recording granted.

Only colors can be saved. The mock's example is a gradient, and the Styles shelf still says the scope holds colors alone: no text styles, no effect styles, and no light and dark resolution of a name, which is the token layer this deliberately stops short of.

A style cannot be applied to more than one layer at a time. With three boxes selected you still set them one at a time, which is the first thing that will feel slow once a document has real components in it.
There is no way to make a style from nothing: you save one from a layer that is already painted. A New Style button on the shelf would be the obvious way in and is not there.

Changing a bound color by some other route (the paint bucket, a paste) quietly unlinks that color rather than refusing the edit, so the row never claims a style it is not wearing. Nothing on screen says the link broke, which is the honest gap in this slice.
Removing a style repaints nothing, on purpose. A person who expects Remove to put colors back the way they were will be surprised, and the button's tooltip is the only place that says so.
